claim: A separately enrolled surviving device-bound administrator can rotate a lost administrator member onto a replacement installation without exporting or escrowing the lost private key. The exact relay denies the lost capability/key and accepts administration from the replacement; recovery still requires either another administrator or the relay host.
proved: The original administrator first enrolls a second independent device-bound administrator under an exact registry revision.
The surviving administrator, using its own key and capability, rotates the original administrator member onto a new public installation enrollment.
Rotation preserves the original member ID and admin role, advances the capability generation, replaces the device key, and stores only capability digests.
The exact relay denies the original capability/key after rotation and accepts both protected-room access and the reserved administration route from the replacement installation.

The product explains that a different surviving administrator can recover onto a replacement installation, that the relay host is required if none survives, and that Syzygy does not export or escrow installation private keys.
notProved: Recovery after every administrator and the relay-host operator are unavailable.
Automatic backup, export, escrow, transfer, or delivery of an installation private key or replacement invitation.
That an administrator installation belongs to an authenticated person or organization.
Packaged physical two-install interaction, public WSS operation, trusted time, or third-party relay behavior.
